title: Loaded Game Day Nachos
seoTitle: Loaded Game Day Nachos | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Chip mountain for the whole couch
subtitle: Chip mountain for the whole couch
description: Chip mountain for the whole couch. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into fine crumbles. Drain excess grease — wet beef makes soggy chips. Stir in taco seasoning and ½ cup water; simmer 5 minutes until saucy.

steps.title: Build chip trays
steps.instruction: Spread chips in a single layer on two full-size sheet pans — double layers steam instead of crisp. Scatter half the cheese over chips.

steps.title: Melt and load
steps.instruction: Broil at 450°F 3–4 minutes until cheese bubbles at the edges. Pull pans, add seasoned beef, remaining cheese, and jalapeños. Broil 2 more minutes until cheese is fully melted.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Top with pico and sour cream at the table — not before, or chips wilt. Loaded Game Day Nachos die fast; make a second tray when the first is half gone.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Build a long snack board: mains down the center, dips and chips at both ends.
Use disposable boats for handhelds so cleanup stays under five minutes after the game.
Line up Loaded Game Day Nachos on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Chip mountain for the whole couch. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
